name: The graded devotional practices of BhG 12.8–12

stages.name: karmaphala-tyāga
stages.gloss: relinquishing the fruit of all actions
stages.description: If unable even to do the Lord's work: resorting to his yoga, self-restrained, relinquish the fruit of all actions (12.11).

stages.name: matkarma-parama
stages.gloss: intent on work for the Lord
stages.description: If unable even in practice: be intent on work for the Lord; doing actions for his sake one attains perfection (12.10).

stages.name: abhyāsa-yoga
stages.description: If unable to fix citta steadily on him: seek to reach him by the yoga of practice (12.9).

stages.name: manas and buddhi in the Lord
stages.gloss: placing manas and buddhi in him
stages.description: Place manas in him alone; let buddhi enter him (12.8).

stages.name: dwelling in the Lord
stages.description: 'You will dwell in me alone thereafter' (12.8).

notes: The text states the sequence from the highest (12.8) downward, each step for one unable to do the previous; it is listed here from entry to goal. 12.12 then ranks knowledge above practice, meditation above knowledge and relinquishment of fruits above meditation, with peace immediately after relinquishment — an order that does not coincide with 12.8–11 and is interpreted variously. Bands are interpretive. The text states the four instructions from the top down (12.8, then 'if you cannot ...' 12.9, 12.10, 12.11); the order here runs upward from the most accessible, as the conditional sequence implies. 12.12 then ranks knowledge above practice, meditation above knowledge and relinquishing the fruit of actions above meditation, with peace following relinquishment — the reverse of the placement of relinquishment in 12.11; commentators commonly read 12.12 as praise of relinquishment. Correspondence bands are left to the interpretation layer.
